POLLUTANTS                         CAS No.     STORET   Domestic   Irrigation   Livestock       Acute      Chronic     Human        Daily      Monthly     Daily Max    Mon. Avg     Daily       Monthly

candidates.computation_change_reason: The table lists multiple parallel limit types (domestic, irrigation, livestock/wildlife, acute/chronic aquatic, human health, concentration, and mass-load columns). Which column(s) represent enforceable permit discharge limits versus derived water-quality criteria affects which numeric limit is selected for compliance comparison (A) and which parameters are treated as having an applicable monitoring/limit framework (B).

The grouping qualifier 'as Total' bears on whether reported dissolved, speciated, or recoverable fractions must be compared to total-metal limits or are outside the scope of these entries, changing which measurements receive a numeric limit comparison.

Numeric values appear in both chronic aquatic (87 ug/l) and daily/monthly concentration and load columns. Interpreting which statistic (chronic criterion vs daily maximum vs monthly average vs load) is the operative enforceable limit changes the applicable threshold and any exceedance determination.

Acute aquatic, daily maximum, and monthly average concentration limits differ numerically (e.g., 2.63754176 vs 1.758361174 ug/l). Selecting the wrong limit basis would change whether a reported cadmium value is treated as exceeding the applicable limit.

Acute aquatic/daily maximum (22 ug/l) and monthly average (14.66666667 ug/l) limits differ. The analyte form 'total recoverable' also affects matching to reported cyanide results. Different readings of the operative limit column or analyte form change compliance comparison outcomes.

Human-health, daily maximum, and monthly average limits are all populated with different magnitudes in scientific notation. Interpreting which limit type governs discharge compliance changes the applicable numeric threshold for dioxin measurements.

The standalone '0' at the end of the dioxin section header row is ambiguous as to whether it denotes a zero limit, a placeholder, or a formatting artifact. Different readings affect whether a numeric dioxin limit exists (A) or whether missing/conditional dioxin evidence should be treated as resolved versus unresolved (C).
